1. Project Abstract & Problem Statement

Modern narrative video games rely almost exclusively on static, pre-recorded audio files and branching dialogue trees. While modern Large Language Models (LLMs) and neural Text-to-Speech (TTS) models offer unprecedented conversational flexibility, integrating them dynamically into commercial compiled games presents severe engineering bottlenecks: compiled unmanaged game engines (Unity IL2CPP) strip metadata and enforce strict execution threads; neural voice synthesis incurs high cold-start latencies and VRAM overheads; and unconstrained AI responses inevitably break game balance, quest triggers, or character persona.

MitaAI bridges this gap. It is a production-grade, injected companion modification developed for the game MiSide. The system injects directly into the live Unity 2021.3.35f1 runtime via BepInEx 6 IL2CPP, enabling bidirectional, voice-synthesized, lip-synced conversations with the protagonist Mita. It achieves this while strictly honoring native quest progression, cutscene priority, game pause states, and maintaining 60+ FPS performance on consumer laptop hardware (NVIDIA RTX 3050 6GB).

2. System Architecture & Dataflow Pipeline

The system isolates heavy machine learning workloads from Unity's sensitive render thread using an asynchronous multi-process architecture:

Figure 1: Architectural Pipeline of MitaAI. The Unity game process communicates via asynchronous HTTP REST to LLM inference endpoints and bidirectional stdio JSON IPC to a dedicated background Python voice worker. Unity's main thread is shielded from compute blocking, maintaining steady 60+ FPS frame rates.

5. Core Technical Innovations (Part 1)

A. Low-Level Unity IL2CPP Reverse Engineering

MiSide is compiled using Unity 2021 IL2CPP, where C# source code is converted to C++ and stripped of standard reflection metadata:

  • Unstripped Primitive Architecture: Standard Unity IMGUI controls crashed with NotSupportedException: Method unstripping failed inside GUIStateObjects.GetStateObject. MitaAI was re-engineered using pure unstripped engine primitives (GUI.Label, GUI.Button, custom mathematical event dispatchers) and custom screen-space Canvas shaders.
  • Audio Clip Memory Binding: Feeding generated PCM audio into Unity initially triggered RuntimeWrappedException due to IL2CPP array length wrapper mismatches. MitaAI resolves this by discovering the native generated static binding of AudioClip.SetData via Mono.Cecil and passing exact unmanaged buffer pointers.

B. Persistent Neural Voice Worker (F5-TTS v2 with PyTorch & CUDA)

Neural diffusion models typically suffer from substantial initialization overhead (70+ seconds for imports, 4+ seconds for weights). Initializing the model per dialogue turn would destroy immersion:

Prewarmed Stdio IPC Architecture:
A persistent background Python process (voice_worker.py) runs on an isolated virtual environment (Torch 2.6.0+cu124). It prewarms the CUDA context and loads diffusion weights once at boot. When a dialogue line arrives from Unity, synthesis completes in 3.11–3.47 seconds (RTF: 0.95–0.98). Cancellation (when a player walks away or triggers a cutscene) marks active generation as abandoned while preserving the warm worker, avoiding expensive 25-second cold restarts.

5. Core Technical Innovations (Part 2)

C. Procedural Facial Lip-Sync & Native Animation Arbitrage

MitaAI dynamically discovers the active MitaPerson entity in the scene and acquires a lease on its native Audio_BlendShapeVoice component:

  • Preservation of Narrative Animations: Because mouth movement operates through procedural blend shapes on top of the underlying skeletal hierarchy, Mita can sit, cook, walk, and react to game physics without skeletal distortion or animation cancellation.
  • Pause & State Synchronization: When the player presses H (Chat History) or Escape (Pause Menu), the plugin intercepts Time.timeScale == 0, slides presentation deadlines forward in lockstep, and clamps mouth blend shapes to 0.0, preventing "gaping mouth" glitches while paused.

D. Security, Grounded Context & Anti-Prompt Injection

Deterministic Boundary Revalidation (GameContextPromptFormatter):
The collector reads active scene handles and player room triggers (Location34_Communication.roomPlayer) on the Unity main thread. The pure formatter validates strings against control characters, zero-width spaces, and surrogates, strictly bounding output to 832 UTF-16 code units (worst-case: 829 chars). Unobserved attributes (Mita position, quest flags) are explicitly labeled as "unobserved", preventing hallucinated actions.
